subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The first permanent President of the All-India Muslim League was:
explanation: Aga Khan III was elected the League's first permanent president in 1907 and held the office until 1913.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The All-India Muslim League was founded during the annual session of the:
explanation: Delegates attending the Educational Conference at Dhaka in December 1906 met separately to found the League.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: One of the original aims of the All-India Muslim League in 1906 was to:
o: Promote loyalty to the British government while protecting Muslim rights
Merge with the Indian National Congress
explanation: The League's early aims were loyalty to the government, protection of Muslim political rights and goodwill with other communities; self-government came later.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Quaid-i-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah joined the All-India Muslim League in:
explanation: Jinnah joined the League in 1913, while remaining a Congress member, and worked to bring the two parties together.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who called Quaid-i-Azam the "Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity"?
explanation: Sarojini Naidu gave Jinnah this title for his efforts to reconcile the Congress and the League, which culminated in the Lucknow Pact.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Quaid-i-Azam left the Indian National Congress in 1920 mainly because he disagreed with:
o: The Congress demand for dominion status
explanation: Jinnah, a constitutionalist, opposed Gandhi's non-cooperation programme adopted at Nagpur in 1920 and left the Congress.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The newspapers Comrade and Hamdard were brought out by:
explanation: Muhammad Ali Jauhar edited the English Comrade and the Urdu Hamdard, both powerful voices of Muslim opinion.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Urdu weekly Al-Hilal (1912) was started by:
explanation: Abul Kalam Azad's Al-Hilal aroused anti-British feeling among Muslims and was banned by the government.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Urdu newspaper "Zamindar" became famous under the editorship of:
explanation: Maulana Zafar Ali Khan made Zamindar of Lahore one of the most influential Muslim papers of the Pakistan Movement era.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Lucknow Pact between the Muslim League and the Congress was concluded in:
explanation: Both parties held their sessions at Lucknow in December 1916 and agreed on joint constitutional demands.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Under the Lucknow Pact, the Congress accepted:
explanation: The Lucknow Pact was the only occasion on which the Congress formally accepted separate electorates for Muslims.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Under the Lucknow Pact, Muslims were to receive what share of elected seats in the central legislature?
explanation: The pact gave Muslims one-third of the elected Indian seats in the Imperial Legislative Council, along with weightage in minority provinces.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Dyarchy in the provinces was introduced by the:
explanation: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (1919 Act) divided provincial subjects into "transferred" ones under Indian ministers and "reserved" ones under the Governor.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre of April 1919 took place in:
explanation: Troops under General Dyer fired on an unarmed crowd in Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, killing hundreds of people.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Khilafat Movement in India was led by:
o: Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan and Mohsin-ul-Mulk
Allama Iqbal and Chaudhry Rahmat Ali
Nawab Salimullah and Aga Khan III
explanation: The Ali Brothers were the leading figures of the Khilafat Movement, which drew Muslims into mass politics.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Khilafat Movement aimed to:
o: Win separate electorates for Indian Muslims
Preserve the Ottoman Caliphate and protect the holy places
explanation: Indian Muslims campaigned after the First World War to save the Turkish Caliphate and keep the holy places under Muslim control.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: During the Hijrat Movement of 1920, thousands of Indian Muslims migrated to:
explanation: Declaring India Dar-ul-Harb, many Muslims sold their property and migrated to Afghanistan, which soon closed its borders; the movement caused great hardship.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1922 after the violent incident at:
explanation: After a mob burned a police station at Chauri Chaura, Gandhi suspended the movement without consulting the Khilafat leaders.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Khilafat Movement lost its purpose when the Caliphate was abolished in 1924 by:
o: Mustafa Kemal Ataturk's government in Turkey
explanation: The Turkish Grand National Assembly under Mustafa Kemal abolished the Caliphate in March 1924, leaving the Indian movement without an object.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Shuddhi and Sangathan, which increased communal tension in the 1920s, were:
o: Hindu movements for reconversion and organisation
explanation: After the Khilafat alliance collapsed, Shuddhi sought to reconvert Muslims to Hinduism and Sangathan to organise Hindus, sharpening Hindu–Muslim rivalry.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In the Delhi Muslim Proposals (1927), Muslim leaders offered to give up:
o: Separate electorates, subject to certain conditions
Their demand for a separate state
Their seats in the central legislature
explanation: Muslim leaders offered joint electorates if Sindh was separated, reforms were introduced in NWFP and Balochistan, and Muslims got one-third of central seats.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Simon Commission (1927) was boycotted in India mainly because:
o: It was headed by a Viceroy
explanation: All seven members of the commission were British parliamentarians, which Indians regarded as an insult.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Nehru Report (1928) was prepared by a committee chaired by:
explanation: The all-parties committee headed by Motilal Nehru drafted the report as India's answer to the Simon Commission.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Nehru Report angered Muslims chiefly because it:
o: Rejected separate electorates in favour of joint electorates
Gave residuary powers to the provinces
Proposed Urdu as the national language
explanation: The report proposed joint electorates, a strong centre and only limited reservation of seats, discarding what Muslims had won in the Lucknow Pact.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: After his amendments to the Nehru Report were rejected at the Calcutta Convention in 1928, Quaid-i-Azam called it:
explanation: Jinnah's remark marked his conclusion that Congress would not accommodate Muslim demands.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Quaid-i-Azam presented his Fourteen Points in:
explanation: Jinnah put forward his Fourteen Points at the League's Delhi session in March 1929.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Quaid-i-Azam's Fourteen Points were a response to the:
explanation: The Fourteen Points set out the minimum Muslim demands after the Nehru Report ignored them.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which of the following was one of Quaid-i-Azam's Fourteen Points?
o: Separation of Sindh from the Bombay Presidency
Vesting residuary powers in the centre
explanation: The Fourteen Points demanded a federal system with residuary powers in the provinces, separate electorates and the separation of Sindh.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Sindh was separated from the Bombay Presidency and made a separate province in:
explanation: Sindh became a separate province on 1 April 1936, fulfilling a long-standing Muslim demand.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The North-West Frontier Province was given the status of a Governor's province, with reforms like other provinces, in:
explanation: NWFP, created in 1901, was raised to a full Governor's province with an elected legislature in 1932, meeting a Muslim demand.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Allama Iqbal's Allahabad Address, which outlined a Muslim state in north-west India, was delivered in:
explanation: Iqbal's presidential address to the League's Allahabad session in December 1930 first gave clear shape to the idea of a Muslim state.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In his Allahabad Address, Allama Iqbal proposed a single Muslim state comprising:
explanation: Iqbal wished to see Punjab, the North-West Frontier Province, Sindh and Balochistan amalgamated into a single state in north-west India.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Allama Iqbal delivered the Allahabad Address as president of the annual session of the:
explanation: Iqbal presided over the annual session of the All-India Muslim League held at Allahabad in December 1930.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In his letters to Quaid-i-Azam (1936–37), Allama Iqbal urged him to:
o: Work for a separate federation of Muslim provinces
explanation: Iqbal wrote that a separate federation of Muslim provinces was the only way to secure peace and save Muslims from domination.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Allama Iqbal's English lectures on Islamic thought were published as:
o: Pakistan or the Partition of India
The Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam
explanation: The Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam collects Iqbal's lectures on ijtihad and the renewal of Muslim thought; The Spirit of Islam is by Ameer Ali.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Allama Iqbal attended which of the Round Table Conferences?
explanation: Iqbal was a Muslim delegate to the Second (1931) and Third (1932) Round Table Conferences in London.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The central idea of self-hood in Allama Iqbal's philosophy is called:
explanation: Iqbal's concept of Khudi calls on the individual to develop the self through action and faith.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The name "Pakistan" was first proposed by Chaudhry Rahmat Ali in his pamphlet:
o: Pakistan or the Partition of India
explanation: Rahmat Ali, a student at Cambridge, issued "Now or Never" in 1933, coining the name Pakistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Round Table Conferences of 1930–32 were held in:
explanation: The British government convened three conferences in London to discuss India's constitutional future.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Congress took part only in the Second Round Table Conference, where it was represented by:
explanation: Gandhi attended the Second Conference (1931) as the sole Congress representative after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Communal Award (1932), which retained separate electorates, was announced by British Prime Minister:
explanation: When Indians could not agree at the Round Table Conferences, Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award allocating seats by community.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who persuaded Quaid-i-Azam in the early 1930s to return from London to lead Muslim politics?
explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan visited Jinnah in London in 1933 and urged him to return; Jinnah came back and revived the League.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The main feature of the Government of India Act 1935 that was actually implemented was:
explanation: Provincial autonomy came into force in 1937, while the proposed federation of provinces and princely states never came into being.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In the provincial elections of 1937, the Muslim League:
o: Could not form a government in any Muslim-majority province
Won a majority in every Muslim-majority province
Swept the Punjab but lost Bengal
explanation: The League did poorly in 1937, winning only a fraction of Muslim seats; regional parties such as the Unionists dominated the Muslim provinces.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Wardha Scheme of education, resented by Muslims, was introduced during:
explanation: The Congress ministries introduced the Wardha Scheme, which Muslims saw as promoting Hindu culture and Gandhian ideas in schools.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Muslims objected to "Bande Mataram" as a national song during Congress rule because it:
o: Came from a novel with anti-Muslim themes
Was the anthem of the Sikhs
explanation: The song was taken from Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's novel Anandamath, which portrayed Muslims as enemies.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Pirpur Report (1938) documented:
o: Muslim grievances under the Congress ministries
explanation: The Muslim League appointed the Pirpur committee, which reported on the hardships of Muslims in Congress-ruled provinces.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Muslim League celebrated the "Day of Deliverance" in December 1939 on:
o: The passing of the Lahore Resolution
The annulment of the partition of Bengal
The resignation of the Congress ministries
The end of the Second World War
explanation: Jinnah called for thanksgiving when the Congress ministries resigned over India's involvement in the war.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Sikandar-Jinnah Pact was concluded in 1937 at the Muslim League session held in:
explanation: At the Lucknow session, Sir Sikandar Hayat agreed that Muslim members of his Unionist Party would join the League.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Lahore Resolution of March 1940 was moved by:
explanation: A. K. Fazlul Haq, the Chief Minister of Bengal, moved the resolution at the League's Lahore session.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Who presided over the historic Lahore session of the All-India Muslim League in 1940?
explanation: Jinnah presided and delivered his address setting out the two-nation case; Iqbal had died in 1938.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Lahore Resolution was passed at:
explanation: The session was held at Minto Park, now Iqbal Park, where the Minar-e-Pakistan stands.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Lahore Resolution was first called the "Pakistan Resolution" by:
explanation: Hindu newspapers derisively labelled it the Pakistan Resolution; the League soon adopted the name.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Lahore Resolution demanded that the Muslim-majority areas in the north-west and east be grouped to form:
o: A single province within an Indian federation
"Independent States" with autonomous and sovereign units
explanation: The 1940 text spoke of "Independent States"; the 1946 Delhi Convention clarified the demand as one sovereign state of Pakistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: At the 1946 Delhi Convention of Muslim League legislators, the resolution calling for one sovereign state of Pakistan was moved by:
explanation: Suhrawardy, then Chief Minister of Bengal, moved the Delhi Resolution in April 1946.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Two-Nation Theory held that the Muslims and Hindus of the subcontinent were:
o: One nation divided only by British policy
Two classes divided by economic interests
Two separate nations with distinct religion, culture and way of life
Two linguistic groups speaking Urdu and Hindi
explanation: The theory, the basis of the Pakistan demand, argued that Muslims were a nation by any definition and needed a homeland of their own.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Sir Stafford Cripps arrived in India with his proposals in:
explanation: Sir Stafford Cripps arrived in March 1942 with proposals meant to win Indian support for the war.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Gandhi described the Cripps proposals as:
explanation: Because the proposals promised dominion status only after the war, Gandhi called them a post-dated cheque.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Cripps proposals were significant for the Muslim League because they:
o: Accepted the creation of Pakistan outright
Gave the League half the seats in the Executive Council
Allowed provinces to stay out of the proposed Indian Union
explanation: The right of provinces not to join the post-war union was an indirect recognition of the Pakistan idea.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Quit India Movement was launched by the Congress in:
explanation: The Congress passed the Quit India resolution in August 1942, and its leaders were promptly arrested.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: At its Karachi session of 1943, the Muslim League adopted the slogan:
explanation: In reply to the Congress's Quit India call, the League asked the British to divide India before leaving.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Gandhi-Jinnah talks of 1944 were held in:
explanation: Gandhi met Jinnah at his Bombay residence in September 1944; the talks failed over the Pakistan demand.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Simla Conference of 1945 failed mainly because:
o: The British refused to hold elections
The League insisted on nominating all Muslim members of the Executive Council
explanation: Lord Wavell ended the conference when the League claimed the sole right to nominate Muslims and the Congress refused.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In the 1945–46 elections to the Central Legislative Assembly, the Muslim League won:
o: A majority of the general seats
explanation: The League's clean sweep of the Muslim seats at the centre, and most provincial Muslim seats, proved its claim to speak for Muslims.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Cabinet Mission of 1946 was headed by:
explanation: The three-member mission was led by the Secretary of State Lord Pethick-Lawrence, with Cripps and A. V. Alexander.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Cabinet Mission Plan proposed:
o: Immediate partition of India into two states
A three-tier union with provinces arranged in three groups
explanation: The plan proposed a weak union centre for defence, foreign affairs and communications, with provinces grouped into sections A, B and C.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Muslim League initially accepted the Cabinet Mission Plan because:
o: It created a sovereign Pakistan at once
Its grouping scheme gave the Muslim-majority areas substantial autonomy
It gave the League control of the central government
explanation: The League saw the compulsory grouping of Muslim-majority provinces as containing the basis of Pakistan; it withdrew after Congress statements undermined the plan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Muslim League decided on "Direct Action" in July 1946 because:
o: Congress statements had undermined the grouping scheme of the Cabinet Mission Plan
The British had refused to hold elections
Gandhi had launched the Quit India Movement
The Radcliffe Award had been announced
explanation: After Nehru declared the Congress free to change the plan, the League withdrew its acceptance and called for Direct Action on 16 August 1946.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In the Interim Government of 1946, Liaquat Ali Khan held the portfolio of:
explanation: As Finance Member, Liaquat presented the 1947 budget, called the "poor man's budget" for its taxes on wealthy businessmen.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which non-Muslim was among the Muslim League's nominees to the Interim Government in 1946?
explanation: The League nominated the Scheduled Caste leader Jogendra Nath Mandal as one of its five members.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In February 1947, British Prime Minister Attlee announced that power would be transferred to Indian hands by:
explanation: Attlee set June 1948 as the deadline; Mountbatten later advanced the transfer to August 1947.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The last Viceroy of British India was:
explanation: Lord Mountbatten replaced Wavell in March 1947 and oversaw the partition and transfer of power.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Under the 3 June Plan, the future of the North-West Frontier Province was decided by:
o: A vote of the provincial assembly
explanation: Because the Congress held a majority in the NWFP assembly, the plan provided for a referendum, which went overwhelmingly for Pakistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Under the 3 June Plan, the question of partitioning Punjab and Bengal was to be decided by:
o: A referendum of all adult voters
The Viceroy in consultation with the princes
Members of their provincial assemblies, voting in two parts
explanation: The legislators of Muslim-majority and non-Muslim-majority districts met separately; a vote for partition by either part would divide the province.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which district of Assam joined East Bengal through a referendum in 1947?
explanation: Sylhet, a Muslim-majority district of Assam, voted to join East Bengal (later East Pakistan).

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The boundary commissions of 1947 for Punjab and Bengal were chaired by:
explanation: Radcliffe chaired both commissions and, as the members disagreed, effectively drew the boundaries himself.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Radcliffe Award gave India a land route to Kashmir by awarding it most of:
explanation: The award of the Muslim-majority tehsils of Gurdaspur to India gave it road access to Jammu and Kashmir.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan came into being under the:
explanation: The British Parliament passed the Indian Independence Act in July 1947, creating the dominions of India and Pakistan from 15 August.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In 1947, British Balochistan decided to join Pakistan through a vote of:
o: The Shahi Jirga and the Quetta Municipality
explanation: Balochistan had no legislature, so the Shahi Jirga and the non-official members of the Quetta Municipality voted for Pakistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In his address to the Constituent Assembly on 11 August 1947, Quaid-i-Azam emphasised:
o: Equal citizenship and religious freedom for all
The adoption of Urdu as the sole state language
explanation: Jinnah told the Assembly that citizens were free to go to their temples, mosques or other places of worship and were all equal citizens of the state.
